text:
arjun: Heads-up: p99 for mixtral-600m jumped ~3x after the kernel-selection tweak last night. Noticed regressions on odd head widths.

perf-bot: Automated profile uploaded: https://ci.internal/redwood/profiles/2130023456 (flamegraph + peak memory).

mira: saw this in staging too. quick numbers from the profile: 
```
model: mixtral-600m
seq_len: 1024
batch: 8
head_dim: 39
kernel chosen: FlashAttention (then fallback to SDPA on some layers)
latency p50/p95/p99: 22ms / 180ms / 390ms (was ~120ms p99 before)
KV cache churn: increased allocations by ~2.2x
```

kenji: key finding from the trace: several forward ops hit alignment path and ended up running SDPA/Triton slowpath due to head stride not being multiple of 8 or 16. Masking kernel was rerouted which forced a different memory layout and triggered cache flushes.

lisa: is this the RoPE scaling interaction we've seen before? I remember a masking edge where scale factor != 1 made masking branch go through a different kernel.

arjun: yes — when RoPE scaling is enabled and head_dim % 8 != 0, kernel-selector picks FlashAttention initially but at runtime some layers fail the mask-compat check and we fallback to SDPA/Triton for those layers. The hybrid run causes extra memcpy + KV reshuffle.

kenji: repro script I ran: 
```bash
python tools/profiler/run_inference.py --model mixtral-600m --seq 1024 --batch 8 --head-dim 39 --rope-scale 1.1 --profile out.json
```
Output shows layer indices [4,9,12] switching kernels mid-run.

mira: actions: 1) add head-dim aware kernel ordering so we avoid triggering a fallback mid-sequence, 2) extend canary to include odd head dims (7,9,13,39), 3) adjust batching heuristic for cached KV workloads.

arjun: propose new heuristic: prefer SDPA (or Triton-safe path) for models where (head_dim % 8 != 0) AND rope_scale != 1.0 when seq_len > 512. Otherwise prefer FlashAttention for layers that pass alignment checks. This prevents mixed-kernel runs.

lisa: +1. Also suggest we log a metric when we change kernel at layer granularity so we can alert on hybrid runs: "kernel_switch_count" per-request.

ops-bot: note: added ticket RW-PLT-3421 to backlog (priority P1).

kenji: small patch sketch for selector (pseudo): 
```python
# kernel_selector.py
if model.rope_scale != 1.0 and (head_dim % 8) != 0 and seq_len > 512:
    preferred = 'sdpa_safe'
else:
    preferred = run_alignment_checks() or 'flash'
```
We should also add a per-layer dry-run that avoids actual memcpy on canary.

mira: batching heuristic: when KV cache present, large batch sizes can amplify fallback cost. Suggest cap batch for cached requests: effective_batch = min(batch, max(1, 4096 // seq_len)) and bias toward smaller batches on odd head widths.

arjun: agreed. Also add unit tests that randomize head_dim in [1..128] with rope_scale variants to ensure selector chooses a uniform kernel (no per-layer flips) or at least limits flips to <=1 per request.

lisa: will you own the canary rollout? Canary plan: route 5% of traffic for 24h, monitor kernel_switch_count, p99 latency, and error rate. If kernel_switch_count > 0.5 per request or p99 regresses >10%, rollback.

arjun: I can run the canary. I'll push the selector patch to feature/headstride-heuristic and add the tests.

perf-bot: perf regression alert rule proposal in PR: trigger when delta(p99) > 8% AND kernel_switch_count per-request > 0.2 within 1h.

kenji: one more note — Qwen variants with head_dim 75 had similar but noisier behavior. Add them to regression matrix.

mira: ok actionable summary: 
- arjun: implement selector change + tests + PR
- lisa: implement metric kernel_switch_count + canary config
- kenji: expand regression matrix and provide repro scripts for qwen/mixtral/llama odd dims
- ops-bot: create canary rollout ticket + monitoring dashboards

arjun: starting work now. I'll post the PR link when ready. Thanks all. :rocket:

lisa: :thumbsup:
